Review completed with 2 findings across 2 agents (2 critical).

⚠️ 2 critical/high severity issues require immediate attention:
  - [CRITICAL] Removal of Template Injection Sanitization in _.template (SecurityAgent)
  - [CRITICAL] Removed security validation allows command injection via `_.template` variable option (LogicAgent)

findings.title: Removal of Template Injection Sanitization in _.template
findings.description: Removal of validation logic that prevented template injection vulnerabilities. The regex `reForbiddenIdentifierChars` and the check `reForbiddenIdentifierChars.test(variable)` were used to sanitize the `variable` option in `_.template`. Without this check, user-supplied input in the `variable` option can inject arbitrary JavaScript code, leading to code execution when the template is rendered.
findings.suggestion: Restore the validation logic. Ensure that the `variable` option is checked against a strict whitelist of valid identifier characters (alphanumeric and underscores) before being used in the generated template source. Do not accept input that can alter the scope of the generated function.

findings.title: Removed security validation allows command injection via `_.template` variable option
findings.description: The diff removes the validation logic that checks the `variable` option in `_.template` for forbidden identifier characters. This check was explicitly implemented to prevent command injection attacks (e.g., passing a string like `'); console.log(password); (` as a variable name). Removing this validation re-introduces a security vulnerability.
findings.suggestion: Restore the validation check: keep the `reForbiddenIdentifierChars` regex, the `INVALID_TEMPL_VAR_ERROR_TEXT` constant, and the `else if` block that throws an error when the variable name contains forbidden characters. This prevents injection attacks through the `variable` option.
